summary: Arthur Waley was a Sinologist, Japanologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at King's College, Cambridge. He worked as Assistant Keeper at the British Museum (1913–1929) and held an Honorary Lectureship in Chinese Poetry at SOAS in 1948.

Arthur William Ryder was an Indologist educated at Harvard, Berlin, and Leipzig under Charles Rockwell Lanman and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He served as Instructor in Sanskrit at Harvard (1902–1906) and Professor of Sanskrit at UC Berkeley (~1906–1938).
Arthur Woollgar Verrall was a scholar who was educated at Wellington College and Trinity College, Cambridge.
Aruna Haldar was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Girindrasekhar Bose and Kedarnath Ojha, and later held a teaching post at Patna University.

Indologist Arunoday Natvarlal Jani earned his Ph.D. from the University of Mumbai under Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt. He served as a professor at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (1967–1980) and directed the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (1975–1981).

Arvind Sharma is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Allahabad, Syracuse, and Harvard. He taught at the University of Queensland and University of Sydney, and was appointed Birks Chair at McGill University in 1994.

Asanga Tilakaratne is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who served as Professor and Head of Buddhist Philosophy at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, University of Kelaniya, from ~1993 to 2009.
Asatoshi Kamiya is a Buddhist studies scholar who was a graduate student at Komazawa University in 1973 and taught at Mejiro Kenshin Junior and Senior High School in 1978.

Asen Balikci earned his PhD from Columbia University in 1956. He worked at the National Museum of Canada (~1957–1964) and served as Professor of Ethnology at the Université de Montréal from 1963 to 1993.

Indologist, linguist, and philosopher Ashok Aklujkar studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University and completed his PhD at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as a professor in Asian Studies at the University of British Columbia (1969–2006).
Ashok Gangadean is a philosopher who completed his PhD at Brandeis University (~1968–1971) and became the Margaret Gest Professor of Global Philosophy at Haverford College in 1981.

Scholar of philosophy, Buddhism, and Indology Ashok Kumar Chatterjee studied at Banaras Hindu University under T. R. V. Murti. He headed the philosophy department at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University (1950–1963) and Banaras Hindu University (1963–1985).
Ashok Kumar Malhotra is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at the East-West Center from ~1963 to 1967.

Ashutosh Mukherjee studied at University of Calcutta and Presidency University. He served on the Calcutta High Court (1904), was Tagore Professor of Law at University of Calcutta (1906–1914), and presided over The Asiatic Society (~1907–1909).

Historian and Indologist Asim Kumar Chatterjee earned his PhD from the University of Calcutta under D. Mukherjee (~1963–1967). He was a senior research fellow there in 1970 and served as a lecturer at Jangipur College.

Asko Parpola is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Pentti Aalto. He worked at the Nordic Institute of Asian Studies and the Academy of Finland, and served as professor at the University of Helsinki (~1982–2004).
Astley John Hilary Goodwin was an archaeologist who studied at St. John's College, Selwyn College, and SOAS University of London, taking up a post at the University of Cape Town in 1923.

Atsuhiko Yoshida was a religious studies scholar and linguist who studied under Georges Dumézil. He held posts at CNRS (~1964–1969) and Seikei University (1970), and served as professor at Gakushuin University in 2006.
Atsushi Ibuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and is attested as a professor at Toyo University in 2015.

Atsushi Kanazawa is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo. He was a lecturer at Meteorological College (1986–1989) and an associate professor at Komazawa University (attested 1996–2003, 2012).
